image_description: A close-up, cropped view of a large marine mammal, identified as a grey whale, swimming at the surface. The image focuses on the dorsal side of the whale's body, showing mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches and a series of dorsal knuckles (humps) instead of a dorsal fin. The surrounding water is blue-green with some white foam/splash.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and blowholes are completely outside the frame or occluded by the angle; only the mid-to-posterior body is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal profile shows a series of small humps (knuckles) rather than a single triangular dorsal fin, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body appears massive and robust, fitting the description of a large baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; texture and coloration match the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the mouth where baleen plates are located is not visible in this dorsal-side shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the ventral/lateral side and are not visible in this top-down/cropped view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution crop allows visualization of the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities and barnacles.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight smudging and lack of crisp definition where the whale's back meets the water line. The splash/foam looks slightly painterly rather than physically simulated, though minor.
The background water has a uniform, slightly soft blur that lacks the complex refraction details of real ocean water, typical of AI generation backgrounds.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another cetacean species (e.g., humpback or right whale) based on skin pattern and dorsal knuckles.
To check for edge bleeding between the whale's dark skin and the lighter water, ensuring the object is topologically sound.
To assess the realism of the water texture and splash effects, which are common failure points in AI-generated marine scenes.
To verify the spatial relationship between the whale and the water surface, ensuring the whale appears submerged/floating correctly rather than pasted on top.

focus_areas: Dorsal knuckle anatomy vs. dorsal fin
Edge sharpness between subject and background
